must_remember: The moment of inertia of a thin uniform ring of mass $M$ and radius $R$ about its central transverse axis is $I = MR^2$.
The moment of inertia of a thin ring about any of its diameters is $I = \frac{1}{2}MR^2$.
The moment of inertia of a ring about a tangent in its own plane is $I = \frac{3}{2}MR^2$.
The moment of inertia of a ring about a tangent perpendicular to its plane is $I = 2MR^2$.
Perpendicular axes theorem states $I_z = I_x + I_y$ and applies strictly to planar (2D) bodies.
Parallel axes theorem states $I = I_{cm} + Md^2$ and applies to any rigid body.

glossary.meaning: Measure of a body's resistance to angular acceleration about a given axis, quantified by $\sum m_i r_i^2$.
Effective distance from the axis of rotation where the entire mass of the body can be assumed to be concentrated, given by $k = \sqrt{I/M}$.
An axis passing through the centre of mass of the ring and perpendicular to its plane.
An axis lying in the plane of the ring and passing through its centre.
